body.body:

### Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509
[CVE-2026-111943](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111943) / [GO-2026-6809](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6809) / [RUSTSEC-2026-0381](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0381.html) / [RUSTSEC-2026-0382](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0382.html) / [RUSTSEC-2026-0383](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0383.html)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action.

To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/cl/851047](https://go.dev/cl/851047)
- [https://go.dev/issue/82345](https://go.dev/issue/82345)
- [https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/66pojueaQek](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/66pojueaQek)

This data is provided by [OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GO-2026-6809) and the [Go Vulnerability Database](https://github.com/golang/vulndb) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://github.com/golang/vulndb#license)).
</details>

body.title: feat: finish the tea 1.0 rewrite — gh-style UX, review fixes, release prep
body.body:
Second half of the tea 1.0 rewrite. #1122–#1126 landed the Cobra command tree, the
services layer on `gitea.dev/sdk`, credentials/Git and the terminal package. This PR
polishes it into the gh-style CLI the reviewers asked for, fixes what a full review of
the branch found, and prepares the 1.0.0 release. It supersedes the revert in #1146.

## What changed

**Output and commands (gh-style)**
- TTY lists with UPPERCASE headers, columns fitted to the terminal, relative times and
  `✓` confirmations on stderr; piped output is TSV without header or color.
- Issue/PR/release/milestone/wiki views render Markdown; `--json`, `--jq` and the field
  list for unknown fields work on every command.
- gh flag and alias parity: `ls`/`rm`, `-L -s -l -a -A -m -t -b -F -e -w -S`, `pr review
  --approve/--request-changes/--comment`, `pr merge` with the repository's defaults,
  `pr ready`, `pr checks` with gh's exit code, `release upload --clobber`,
  `run watch/download`, `repo rename/unarchive/fork --remote`, `auth login/status/switch`,
  `doctor`, `tea status` and `tea api --verbose`.
- Grouped help, help topics (`environment`, `exit-codes`, `formatting`), flag-value
  completion and "did you mean" for unknown flags.

**Review fixes (about 150 items, each with a regression test)**
- Security: terminal escape sequences from server text (Markdown character references,
  PR titles in messages, `auth status`, `notification watch`, JSON/jq output) can no
  longer reach the terminal; `auth logout` only asks Git to forget tea's own credential.
- Behavior: `team edit --unit` keeps the access of read/write teams and the owner team
  cannot be renamed; `release edit --draft false` (0.16 syntax) is refused instead of
  reversing the release; `release upload --clobber` uploads before deleting; re-login keeps
  SSH settings; `pr merge` no longer deletes a head branch Gitea kept; `pr checkout`,
  `pr clean` and the no-argument `pr` commands no longer pick an unrelated fork branch;
  `review_decision` ignores comment-only reviews; `comment list`/`pr review list` page
  correctly; wiki edits no longer overwrite an existing page.
- Where gh solves the same problem the fix follows gh (for example `auth status --json`
  always exits 0, a bare `GITEA_TOKEN` overrides stored accounts, `pr reopen|close|view`
  find closed and merged PRs by branch, `release create --verify-tag`).

**Folded in from open PRs**
- #1021 (find the Gitea remote among all remotes), #1144 (load the `pr create`/`issue
  create` form data concurrently) and #1145 (single-request template lookup), re-implemented
  on the new architecture.
- In a fork clone tea now prefers `upstream` over a tracked `origin` (#338).

**Release prep**
- goldmark and `golang.org/x` updated (the previous goldmark was flagged by govulncheck);
  stale `retract` removed; snap build handles lightweight tags; version fallback for
  builds without ldflags; man pages include the help topics; `CHANGELOG.md` has a drafted
  1.0.0 section; the integration tests match the 1.0 behavior.

## Breaking changes and migration

Everything that differs from tea 0.16 is documented in `docs/migration-1.0.md` (renamed
commands, changed short flags such as `pr create -b`, removed flags, config split, Gitea 28
requirement). This PR adds the remaining notes found during review.

## Not in this PR

- `flake.lock` still pins an old nixpkgs (needs `nix flake update nixpkgs`).
- Larger features stay for 1.1: `issue export/import` (#132), project boards (#435), TLS
  client certificates (#451), custom login headers (#990), package commands (#843).
- Open design questions: `team edit --permission` on Gitea 28.0.0, atomic topic updates in
  `repo edit`, `--repo NAME` matching a local directory name.

## Issues

body.title: perf(pr): probe pull request template paths concurrently
body.body:
Thanks again for reviewing these! This is the follow-up mentioned in #1144.

> **Note: this is a bigger change than #1144.** It changes how the template lookup behaves on the wire: every lookup now sends all six requests instead of stopping at the first match, and the existing tests that asserted the early stop are updated accordingly. Which template is returned does not change.

## Problem

`Pulls.Template` probes six paths one after another. A repository without a pull request template pays for six sequential 404s, about 1.2 s against gitea.com. With #1144 applied, this is the longest remaining step before the interactive form appears.

## Changes

- Probe all six template paths concurrently.
- Decide the result in the existing priority order: the highest-priority match wins, and an error is reported only when every higher-priority path is missing, exactly as before.
- Both callers benefit: the interactive `tea pr create` form and `tea pr create --editor`.

## Trade-off

- Fewer round trips one after another: the lookup now takes as long as the slowest single request instead of the sum of up to six.
- More requests per lookup: always six. Previously a repository with a root-level template needed only one.

If always sending six requests is not acceptable, an alternative is to probe in priority order and cancel the lower-priority requests once a higher-priority one matches. That needs more code, so I kept this version simple.

## Measurements

Time from start until the first prompt, `tea pr create` against a gitea.com repository with push access and no PR template, median of 10 alternating runs:

| | median |
|---|---|
| `main` | 3361 ms |
| this PR | 2028 ms |
| this PR + #1144 | 1210 ms |

## Testing

- `go test -race ./...`
- `TestPullTemplateLookup` now expects six requests in every case and adds cases for a match before an error and an error before a match.
- New `TestPullTemplateProbesConcurrently` verifies that all probes are in flight at the same time.
- The two PRs touch different files and merge cleanly in either order.
- Manually ran `tea pr create` against gitea.com.

body.title: perf(pr create): load interactive form data concurrently
body.body:
Thanks for the Cobra/services rework — having all form data loaded in one place made this a small, contained change.

## Problem

Before the interactive `tea pr create` form appears, tea loads its data strictly one request after another:

1. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` for the default branch
2. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` again for push permissions
3. assignees
4. milestones
5. labels
6. the pull request template, probing up to six paths

Against gitea.com this takes about 3 s before the first prompt shows up.

## Changes

- Add `Pulls.CreateChoices`, which fetches the repository once and reuses it for both the default branch and the push permission check.
- Load the pull request template concurrently with the selectables.
- Load assignees, milestones and labels concurrently.
- `Issues.CreateSelectables` loads issue templates concurrently with the selectables, so `tea issue create` benefits as well.

The template lookup itself is unchanged: paths are still probed in priority order and the lookup stops at the first match. Form fields, defaults and error handling are unchanged.

## Measurements

Time from start until the first prompt, `tea pr create` against a gitea.com repository with push access and no PR template, median of 10 alternating runs:

| | median |
|---|---|
| `main` | 3066 ms |
| this PR | 2238 ms |

## Testing

- `go test -race ./...`
- New tests cover a single repository fetch, the template being read from the default branch, error propagation, and that template/assignees/milestones/labels requests are in flight at the same time.
- Manually ran `tea pr create` against gitea.com.

body.title: docs: describe the gh-style output, aliases and flags in the 1.0 guide
body.body:
Part 12/12 of the tea 1.0 UX rework: gh-style output (headers, relative times, TSV when piped), completion of flag values, gh flag and alias parity, and rendered Markdown, after review feedback on the 1.0 stack. Builds on #1142: only the last commit is new.

**Stack** (each PR targets `main` and builds, tests and lints on its own; commands that have not moved yet keep compiling through temporary legacy files that part 11 removes):

1. #1132 Security and data-loss fixes
2. #1133 Terminal output foundation
3. #1134 CLI core: help, completion, errors
4. #1135 Orgs, teams and admin
5. #1136 Repositories and branches
6. #1137 Actions
7. #1138 Auth, config, api and doctor
8. #1139 Releases and wiki
9. #1140 Pull requests
10. #1141 Issues and comments
11. #1142 Labels, milestones and time
12. #1143 Docs and strict help tests ← this PR

## Changes

Update the 1.0 migration guide, README, contributing notes and example workflows for the new output, aliases and flags, and require help texts and examples on every command now that every command has them. The usage-error table covers every command again.
